title: Worldwide Youth in Science and Engineering (WYSE)
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Grainger College of Engineering
description: A Grainger College of Engineering outreach umbrella offering several pre-college STEM summer tracks at UIUC. 'Exploring Your Options' (EYO) is a week-long residential engineering-exploration camp for rising 9th-12th graders, invite-focused on students from traditionally excluded populations in STEM, introducing roughly 11 engineering disciplines (aerospace, bioengineering, chemical, civil, computer science, electrical & computer, industrial systems, materials science, mechanical, nuclear) through hands-on activities led by engineering students and faculty; 2026 sessions ran June 21-27 (ISR residence hall) and July 12-18 (Hendrick House). The flagship 'Young Scholars Summer STEMM Research Program' is a 6-week authentic mentored research experience for rising 10th-12th graders from Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Missouri, Iowa, and Wisconsin, placing students in university labs across fields such as cancer immunology, neuroscience, artificial intelligence, physics, quantum mechanics, and bioengineering (SpHERES track for medicine/engineering, GEnYuS track for Grainger Engineering research); participants complete 30-35 research hours per week plus weekly seminars on scientific communication and college preparation, culminating in a poster symposium. WYSE also runs a separate 'Digital Scholars' computing-skills program in Chicago through the Discovery Partners Institute.
residency_restrictions: Young Scholars Summer STEMM Research Program is limited to residents of Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Missouri, Iowa, and Wisconsin; EYO camp draws primarily from the broader Midwest region on an outreach basis and is open to all applicants.
application_requirements: EYO Camp: outreach-focused nomination/application emphasizing underrepresented populations in STEM
Young Scholars: application materials used to assign a research track (SpHERES or GEnYuS)
selectivity_evidence: Official pages state EYO's 2026 sessions were full shortly after opening (30-person residence-hall cohorts) and that Young Scholars assigns students to one of two limited research tracks based on application review; no acceptance rate is published for either track.
current_cycle_label: Summer 2026: EYO Session 1 June 21-27 (ISR), Session 2 July 12-18 (Hendrick House); Young Scholars STEMM Research June 14-July 31 (online orientation late May/June 10-11, in-person orientation June 15-16, research June 17-July 30, final symposium July 31). Both EYO and Young Scholars applications for 2026 are now closed/full.

title: WPI Frontiers
description: A two-week, non-credit residential pre-college program on WPI's Worcester, Massachusetts campus for rising 10th, 11th, and 12th graders, offered as Frontiers I and Frontiers II sessions. Students choose a STEM or Business major paired with a humanities, arts, or business minor, taking lab-based classes taught by WPI-affiliated instructors alongside college-prep workshops, field trips, and social activities that give an all-encompassing preview of college life (students live in WPI residence halls with current-student mentors). The program emphasizes hands-on, project-based STEM exploration rather than passive lecture instruction, and is run out of WPI's Office of Pre-Collegiate Outreach Programs.
application_requirements: online application with personal identifying information
TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo English Test for international applicants only
selectivity_evidence: Official admissions pages describe a holistic review of short-response essays, an activities list, and transcripts, but do not publish an acceptance rate or minimum GPA.
current_cycle_label: 2027 cycle: Frontiers I July 5-16, 2027; Frontiers II July 18-30, 2027. Applications for Summer 2027 open in early December 2026; the most recently completed cycle (Summer 2026) has already concluded as of this research.

title: Case Western Reserve University Online Pre-College Program
description: A fully online, largely asynchronous pre-college enrichment program for students age 13 and up, run by Case Western Reserve University through the Prelum (Kaplan) partner-university platform and supported directly by CWRU staff (support@precollege.case.edu). Six courses are offered across STEM, medicine, and business: 'Inside the Brain and Nervous System' (neuroscience/medicine), 'From 2D Sketch to 3D Model' (engineering), 'The Origins of Life' (astrophysics/evolutionary biology), an introduction to medicine's future (biomedical engineering), and 'The Business of Helping Others' (social entrepreneurship), among others. Each course runs 20-30 hours of multimedia lessons and assignments over a 2- or 4-week session offered on a rolling, year-round basis via the Canvas learning platform, taught with video lessons from CWRU instructors and mentor support, culminating in a final project and a Certificate of Completion for students who finish at least 70% of coursework. The program is explicitly non-credit and does not confer admissions preference at CWRU, but adds a documented higher-education experience to a student's record.
application_requirements: simplified online application with a short written response
no transcripts or letters of recommendation required
selectivity_evidence: Official FAQ states the application is a simplified online form with a short response and explicitly does not require transcripts or recommendation letters, and that decisions are prompt -- indicating open enrollment rather than competitive selection.
current_cycle_label: Rolling, year-round enrollment; 2- and 4-week course sessions run continuously rather than on a single annual summer cycle.

title: Wharton Global Youth Program: Future of the Business World (FBW)
organization: The Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania (Wharton Global Youth Program)
description: A fully online, two-week summer business program for high school students in grades 9-12 worldwide, run by the Wharton Global Youth Program. Each two-week session pairs live daily instruction led by Wharton faculty (students pick one of two live lecture time blocks, 8-10am or 1-3pm EDT, plus a recitation block, to accommodate global time zones) with independent work, small-group collaborative projects with peers around the world, and original real-time business simulations covering innovation, design thinking, market research, scenario planning, and leadership communication. The program culminates in a capstone project in which students make predictions about the future of the business world, and all participants who complete requirements earn a Wharton Global Youth Certificate of Completion plus digital badge; students also gain access to the Wharton Youth Network alumni community.
application_requirements: optional need-based financial-aid application (checked in main application, due Feb 4, 2026)
selectivity_evidence: Official program page states selection is based on 'academic excellence and genuine interest in developing business acumen' but does not publish an acceptance rate or list required supplemental materials beyond the application and fee.
current_cycle_label: Most recently confirmed cycle: Summer 2026, Session 1 June 15-26 and Session 2 July 6-17, priority deadline January 28, 2026 (rolling thereafter); this cycle has already concluded as of this research and 2027 dates were not yet posted on the official page.

title: Penn Medicine Summer Program for High School Students
organization: Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania (Penn Medicine)
description: A four-week residential summer program at the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine for rising high school juniors and seniors interested in medicine, run by Penn Medicine in partnership with the BOLD Summers application platform. The curriculum is modeled after the first year of Penn Med classes, structured so 'each week represents a year in medical school': week one covers basic medical studies, week two covers specialties, week three covers surgery and psychiatry, and week four lets students pursue a specialty of their choice. Students get hands-on exposure through simulations and live demonstrations (including manikin-based intubation practice) taught by Penn Medicine physicians and faculty, with the potential to observe a live surgery, and take weekend excursions to destinations such as New York City, the Jersey Shore, Washington DC, Hershey Park, or Six Flags. Penn Medicine's own program lead states participants 'actually do things that some of our actual medical students haven't experienced yet.'
application_requirements: completed high-school-level biology course prior to program start
online application via BOLD Summers portal
selectivity_evidence: The official application requires a specific 300-350 word personal essay and detailed extracurricular descriptions; applications submitted after the February 26, 2026 priority deadline are reviewed beginning in April on a rolling, space-available basis, indicating capacity-limited but not single-cutoff selection. No acceptance rate is published.
current_cycle_label: Most recently confirmed cycle: Summer 2026, June 28-July 24, 2026; applications opened November 17, 2025 with a February 26, 2026 priority deadline and rolling review after that date. This cycle has already concluded as of this research.

title: Idyllwild Arts Summer Program (High School Intensives)
organization: Idyllwild Arts Academy / Idyllwild Arts Foundation
description: A set of immersive, discipline-specific summer intensives for teens (roughly ages 12-17) held on the Idyllwild Arts Academy campus in the San Jacinto Mountains of Southern California (elevation 5,000+ feet), taught by professional artist-teachers across Visual Arts, Native American Arts, Fashion Design, Music, Dramatic Arts, Film & Digital Media, Dance, and Creative Writing. As a verified representative example, the 2026 Dance Intensive (July 12-25) is a two-week, audition-based program requiring at least three years of prior training in ballet, modern, or jazz; students train 6-8 hours daily in Ballet, Pointe, Jazz, Modern, Hip Hop, Musical Theatre Dance, and Choreography, culminating in a public student recital. Other 2026 tracks include the four-week Filmmaking Intensive (June 28-July 25, ages 14-17), Fashion Design Intensive (two two-week sessions), Instrumental Artist's Intensive (strings/piano feeding into chamber music), Musical Theatre Intensive, and Creative Writing Intensive -- each with its own audition or portfolio requirements, dates, and pricing.
application_requirements: discipline-specific audition video or portfolio (e.g., one-minute dance audition video via Submittable)
rolling admission until program capacity is reached
selectivity_evidence: The Dance Intensive requires an audition video and at least three years of prior formal training in ballet, modern, or jazz, and caps enrollment at 30 students; admission is rolling until capacity is reached rather than judged against a single acceptance-rate figure, which the official site does not publish.

title: Boston University Tanglewood Institute (BUTI)
organization: Boston University College of Fine Arts, in partnership with the Boston Symphony Orchestra
description: One of the most prestigious and longest-running summer conservatory-level training programs for pre-college musicians in the United States, held at Tanglewood in Lenox, Massachusetts -- the summer home of the Boston Symphony Orchestra -- with 2026 marking BUTI's 60th anniversary season. BUTI offers 25 individual programs for instrumentalists, singers, and composers spanning all orchestral instruments, piano, voice, harp, composition, and electroacoustic composition, with each track running 2 to 8 weeks depending on discipline and level. More than 400 students arrive annually from across the country and around the world for daily ensemble rehearsals, private lessons with BUTI faculty and BSO guest artists, chamber-music coaching, and multiple public performances, with faculty drawn from the Boston Symphony Orchestra, Boston University, and the BUTI alumni community.
selectivity_evidence: BUTI is widely recognized as one of the most competitive summer training programs for pre-college musicians in the US, drawing 400+ applicants annually from around the world through a live-or-recorded audition process; the official site does not publish a numeric acceptance rate.
